Programming traces and repairs

Unit 1 · Week 15 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the consolidation chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Programming traces and repairs

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Trace pseudocode and verify a targeted correction. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

2. Retrieval and explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval, then partner comparison

A running sum normally starts at zero before the loop. For first maximum, start from a real element after an empty check and update only for a greater value. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

3. Trace a first maximum

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and teacher explanation

Use a strict greater-than comparison. Equality keeps the earlier index. The total is 10, a separate calculation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

4. A reset inside the loop

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, model and explain

The faulty result is 5 because total is reset each pass. Move initialisation before the loop and retest to obtain 7. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

5. Pseudocode transfer

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

Use station B’s supplied pseudocode. Do not silently assume all pseudocode conventions use identical endpoint rules. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

6. Independent practice

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application with optional support

Keep the failed trace and changed example. A correct maximum on positive data alone will not expose an initial-zero bug. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

7. A choice to explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Whole-class response and justification

A. The correct maximum is -3. An index initialised to zero is a different idea from a maximum value initialised to zero. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

8. Exit explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual reflection and fresh explanation

Require a causal explanation and discriminating test, not merely a rewritten line. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#consolidation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.
